NKJV.1: Moreover the LORD answered Job, and said:
NKJV.2: “Shall the one who contends with the Almighty correct Him? He who rebukes God, let him answer it.”
NKJV.3: Then Job answered the LORD and said:
NKJV.4: “Behold,  I am vile; What shall I answer You?  I lay my hand over my mouth.
NKJV.5: Once I have spoken, but I will not answer; Yes, twice, but I will proceed no further.”
NKJV.6: Then the LORD answered Job out of the whirlwind, and said:
NKJV.7: “Now  prepare yourself like a man;  I will question you, and you shall answer Me:
NKJV.8: “Would  you indeed annul My judgment? Would you condemn Me that you may be justified?
NKJV.9: Have you an arm like God? Or can you thunder with a voice like His?
NKJV.10: Then adorn yourself with majesty and splendor, And array yourself with glory and beauty.
NKJV.11: Disperse the rage of your wrath; Look on everyone who is proud, and humble him.
NKJV.12: Look on everyone who is proud, and bring him low; Tread down the wicked in their place.
NKJV.13: Hide them in the dust together, Bind their faces in hidden darkness.
NKJV.14: Then I will also confess to you That your own right hand can save you.
NKJV.15: “Look now at the behemoth, which I made along with you; He eats grass like an ox.
NKJV.16: See now, his strength is in his hips, And his power is in his stomach muscles.
NKJV.17: He moves his tail like a cedar; The sinews of his thighs are tightly knit.
NKJV.18: His bones are like beams of bronze, His ribs like bars of iron.
NKJV.19: He is the first of the ways of God; Only He who made him can bring near His sword.
NKJV.20: Surely the mountains yield food for him, And all the beasts of the field play there.
NKJV.21: He lies under the lotus trees, In a covert of reeds and marsh.
NKJV.22: The lotus trees cover him with their shade; The willows by the brook surround him.
NKJV.23: Indeed the river may rage, Yet he is not disturbed; He is confident, though the Jordan gushes into his mouth,
NKJV.24: Though he takes it in his eyes, Or one pierces his nose with a snare.

NASB.1: Then the LORD said to Job,
NASB.2: 'Will the faultfinder contend with the Almighty? Let him who reproves God answer it.'
NASB.3: Then Job answered the LORD and said,
NASB.4: 'Behold, I am insignificant; what can I reply to You? I lay my hand on my mouth.
NASB.5: 'Once I have spoken, and I will not answer; Even twice, and I will add nothing more.'
NASB.6: Then the LORD answered Job out of the storm and said,
NASB.7: 'Now gird up your loins like a man; I will ask you, and you instruct Me.
NASB.8: 'Will you really annul My judgment? Will you condemn Me that you may be justified?
NASB.9: 'Or do you have an arm like God, And can you thunder with a voice like His?
NASB.10: 'Adorn yourself with eminence and dignity, And clothe yourself with honor and majesty.
NASB.11: 'Pour out the overflowings of your anger, And look on everyone who is proud, and make him low.
NASB.12: 'Look on everyone who is proud, [and] humble him, And tread down the wicked where they stand.
NASB.13: 'Hide them in the dust together; Bind them in the hidden [place].
NASB.14: 'Then I will also confess to you, That your own right hand can save you.
NASB.15: 'Behold now, Behemoth, which I made as well as you; He eats grass like an ox.
NASB.16: 'Behold now, his strength in his loins And his power in the muscles of his belly.
NASB.17: 'He bends his tail like a cedar; The sinews of his thighs are knit together.
NASB.18: 'His bones are tubes of bronze; His limbs are like bars of iron.
NASB.19: 'He is the first of the ways of God; Let his maker bring near his sword.
NASB.20: 'Surely the mountains bring him food, And all the beasts of the field play there.
NASB.21: 'Under the lotus plants he lies down, In the covert of the reeds and the marsh.
NASB.22: 'The lotus plants cover him with shade; The willows of the brook surround him.
NASB.23: 'If a river rages, he is not alarmed; He is confident, though the Jordan rushes to his mouth.
NASB.24: 'Can anyone capture him when he is on watch, With barbs can anyone pierce [his] nose?

ESV.1: And the LORD said to Job:
ESV.2: “Shall a faultfinder contend with the Almighty? He who argues with God, let him answer it.”

ESV.4: “Behold, I am of small account; what shall I answer you? I lay my hand on my mouth.
ESV.5: I have spoken once, and I will not answer; twice, but I will proceed no further.”
ESV.6: Then the LORD answered Job out of the whirlwind and said:
ESV.7: “Dress for action  like a man; I will question you, and you make it known to me.
ESV.8: Will you even put me in the wrong? Will you condemn me that you may be in the right?
ESV.9: Have you an arm like God, and can you thunder with a voice like his?
ESV.10: “Adorn yourself with majesty and dignity; clothe yourself with glory and splendor.
ESV.11: Pour out the overflowings of your anger, and look on everyone who is proud and abase him.
ESV.12: Look on everyone who is proud and bring him low and tread down the wicked where they stand.
ESV.13: Hide them all in the dust together; bind their faces in the world below.
ESV.14: Then will I also acknowledge to you that your own right hand can save you.
ESV.15: “Behold, Behemoth,  which I made as I made you; he eats grass like an ox.
ESV.16: Behold, his strength in his loins, and his power in the muscles of his belly.
ESV.17: He makes his tail stiff like a cedar; the sinews of his thighs are knit together.
ESV.18: His bones are tubes of bronze, his limbs like bars of iron.
ESV.19: “He is the first of the works  of God; let him who made him bring near his sword!
ESV.20: For the mountains yield food for him where all the wild beasts play.
ESV.21: Under the lotus plants he lies, in the shelter of the reeds and in the marsh.
ESV.22: For his shade the lotus trees cover him; the willows of the brook surround him.
ESV.23: Behold, if the river is turbulent he is not frightened; he is confident though Jordan rushes against his mouth.
ESV.24: Can one take him by his eyes,  or pierce his nose with a snare?

NLT.1: Then the LORD said to Job,
NLT.2:
“Do you still want to argue with the Almighty?
You are God’s critic, but do you have the answers?”
NLT.3: Then Job replied to the LORD,
NLT.4:
“I am nothing — how could I ever find the answers?
I will cover my mouth with my hand.
NLT.5:
I have said too much already.
I have nothing more to say.”
NLT.6: Then the LORD answered Job from the whirlwind:
NLT.7:
“Brace yourself like a man,
because I have some questions for you,
and you must answer them.
NLT.8:
“Will you discredit my justice
and condemn me just to prove you are right?
NLT.9:
Are you as strong as God?
Can you thunder with a voice like his?
NLT.10:
All right, put on your glory and splendor,
your honor and majesty.
NLT.11:
Give vent to your anger.
Let it overflow against the proud.
NLT.12:
Humiliate the proud with a glance;
walk on the wicked where they stand.
NLT.13:
Bury them in the dust.
Imprison them in the world of the dead.
NLT.14:
Then even I would praise you,
for your own strength would save you.
NLT.15:
“Take a look at Behemoth,
which I made, just as I made you.
It eats grass like an ox.
NLT.16:
See its powerful loins
and the muscles of its belly.
NLT.17:
Its tail is as strong as a cedar.
The sinews of its thighs are knit tightly together.
NLT.18:
Its bones are tubes of bronze.
Its limbs are bars of iron.
NLT.19:
It is a prime example of God’s handiwork,
and only its Creator can threaten it.
NLT.20:
The mountains offer it their best food,
where all the wild animals play.
NLT.21:
It lies under the lotus plants,
hidden by the reeds in the marsh.
NLT.22:
The lotus plants give it shade
among the willows beside the stream.
NLT.23:
It is not disturbed by the raging river,
not concerned when the swelling Jordan rushes around it.
NLT.24:
No one can catch it off guard
or put a ring in its nose and lead it away.

MSG.2:
"Now what do you have to say for yourself?
Are you going to haul me, the Mighty One, into court and press
charges?"
MSG.4:
"I'm speechless, in awe—words fail me.
I should never have opened my mouth!
MSG.5:
I've talked too much, way too much.
I'm ready to shut up and listen."
MSG.6: God addressed Job next from the eye of the storm, and this is what he said:
MSG.7:
"I have some more questions for you,
and I want straight answers.
MSG.8:
"Do you presume to tell me what I'm doing wrong?
Are you calling me a sinner so you can be a saint?
MSG.9:
Do you have an arm like my arm?
Can you shout in thunder the way I can?
MSG.10:
Go ahead, show your stuff.
Let's see what you're made of, what you can do.
MSG.11:
Unleash your outrage.
Target the arrogant and lay them flat.
MSG.12:
Target the arrogant and bring them to their knees.
Stop the wicked in their tracks—make mincemeat of them!
MSG.13:
Dig a mass grave and dump them in it—
faceless corpses in an unmarked grave.
MSG.14:
I'll gladly step aside and hand things over to you—
you can surely save yourself with no help from me!
MSG.15:
"Look at the land beast, Behemoth. I created him as well as you.
Grazing on grass, docile as a cow—
MSG.16:
Just look at the strength of his back,
the powerful muscles of his belly.
MSG.17:
His tail sways like a cedar in the wind;
his huge legs are like beech trees.
MSG.18:
His skeleton is made of steel,
every bone in his body hard as steel.
MSG.19:
Most magnificent of all my creatures,
but I still lead him around like a lamb!
MSG.20:
The grass-covered hills serve him meals,
while field mice frolic in his shadow.
MSG.21:
He takes afternoon naps under shade trees,
cools himself in the reedy swamps,
MSG.22:
Lazily cool in the leafy shadows
as the breeze moves through the willows.
MSG.23:
And when the river rages he doesn't budge,
stolid and unperturbed even when the Jordan goes wild.
MSG.24:
But you'd never want him for a pet—
you'd never be able to housebreak him!

his limbs like rods of iron.
NIV.19:
He ranks first among the works of God,
yet his Maker can approach him with his sword.
NIV.20:
The hills bring him their produce,
and all the wild animals play nearby.
NIV.21:
Under the lotus plants he lies,
hidden among the reeds in the marsh.
NIV.22:
The lotuses conceal him in their shadow;
the poplars by the stream surround him.
NIV.23:
When the river rages, he is not alarmed;
he is secure, though the Jordan should surge against his mouth.
NIV.24:
Can anyone capture him by the eyes,
or trap him and pierce his nose?

NET.2: “Will the one who contends with the Almighty correct him? Let the person who accuses God give him an answer!”
NET.4: “Indeed, I am completely unworthy — how could I reply to you? I put my hand over my mouth to silence myself.
NET.5: I have spoken once, but I cannot answer; twice, but I will say no more.”
NET.6: Then the LORD answered Job from the whirlwind:
NET.7: “Get ready for a difficult task like a man. I will question you and you will inform me!
NET.8: Would you indeed annul my justice? Would you declare me guilty so that you might be right?
NET.9: Do you have an arm as powerful as God’s, and can you thunder with a voice like his?
NET.10: Adorn yourself, then, with majesty and excellency, and clothe yourself with glory and honor!
NET.11: Scatter abroad the abundance of your anger. Look at every proud man and bring him low;
NET.12: Look at every proud man and abase him; crush the wicked on the spot!
NET.13: Hide them in the dust together, imprison them in the grave.
NET.14: Then I myself will acknowledge to you that your own right hand can save you.
NET.15: “Look now at Behemoth, which I made as I made you; it eats grass like the ox.
NET.16: Look at its strength in its loins, and its power in the muscles of its belly.
NET.17: It makes its tail stiff like a cedar, the sinews of its thighs are tightly wound.
NET.18: Its bones are tubes of bronze, its limbs like bars of iron.
NET.19: It ranks first among the works of God, the One who made it has furnished it with a sword.
NET.20: For the hills bring it food, where all the wild animals play.
NET.21: Under the lotus trees it lies, in the secrecy of the reeds and the marsh.
NET.22: The lotus trees conceal it in their shadow; the poplars by the stream conceal it.
NET.23: If the river rages, it is not disturbed, it is secure, though the Jordan should surge up to its mouth.
NET.24: Can anyone catch it by its eyes, or pierce its nose with a snare?
